blocks.h2: Getting a New Heater Into an Old Basement
blocks.body: Old Chicago basements weren't built with today's appliances in mind. Stairs can be steep and narrow, with a turn at the bottom. Doorways can be low. Before we quote, we measure the path from the street to the heater's spot. If a standard tank won't fit, we'll suggest a shorter or narrower model, or a tankless unit that carries in easily. You won't find out on install day that it doesn't fit.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a New Water Heater
blocks.body: Size, fuel and venting come first. Shared chimneys may need a liner. Narrow stairs and low ceilings add labor. We check everything and quote one flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Will a new heater fit down my basement stairs?
items.answer: We measure before quoting and recommend a model that fits.

items.q: Do I need a chimney liner?
items.answer: Sometimes, if the heater is the only appliance left on the chimney or the flue is oversized. We test it.

items.q: Can you replace both heaters in a two-flat at once?
items.answer: Yes, usually in the same visit.

items.q: Do you take the old heater?
items.answer: Yes, including carrying it up the stairs.

items.q: Can a water heater go in a closet?
items.preview: Often, with the right model and venting.
items.answer: Often, if there's proper venting, combustion air and a drain pan.

items.q: Do you install heat pump water heaters?
items.answer: They need space and airflow. Ask us whether your basement is a good fit.

items.q: How much does water heater installation cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on size, type and venting. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size, fuel type, venting and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
